title: The Orbit of Kepler Reach
premise: Mirabel Vasquez has spent twelve years as a cargo navigator in Kepler Reach, hiding the truth that she is a backup copy of the colony's dead founder, one of seven sleeping in the hold of her ship. When the colony's children begin dreaming her original's memories, both rival fleets converge on Kepler Reach, each believing the other has stolen resurrection technology. Mirabel must maintain the lie that no backups exist, brokering a fragile truce, until the dreams force her to choose between erasing herself forever or revealing what she is. In the end, she wakes the other six, and the colonists—led by the children who dreamed her home—claim them not as weapons but as family.
about_author: Xanthe Delacroix is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who traded flight manifests for fiction after a decade spent watching cargo drift between contested stations. They write about people who keep systems running and secrets buried, and live somewhere with excellent views of passing satellites.

chapters.title: The Hold Below
chapters.summary: Mirabel navigates a routine run through contested space while suppressing the hum of the six backup pods in her hold. When a child at the docking bay greets her by her founder-name, Vasquez-Prime, she dismisses it as coincidence. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine—the past she buried knocking politely on the hull.

chapters.title: Shared Sky
chapters.summary: Dozens of colony children now dream identical memories: a launch, a fire, a woman singing in an airlock. Both fleets accuse each other of running illegal consciousness copies and mass toward Kepler Reach. Mirabel realizes the dreams are leaking from her own suppressed pod-link. POV: Mirabel, with interludes from ten-year-old Sefi, a dreamer. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening into responsibility.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Mirabel brokers a tense parley aboard her ship, feeding both fleets fabricated sensor data to hide the pods. But Sefi stows aboard, finds the hold, and recognizes Mirabel's face from the dreams. The fleets' scanners brush the ship; the truce frays. POV: alternating Mirabel and Sefi. Emotional beat: climax—exposure imminent, and Mirabel must decide whether the lie or the lives inside it matter more.

chapters.title: Kepler Reach
chapters.summary: Rather than let the fleets discover the pods through violence, Mirabel broadcasts the truth herself and wakes the six backups before the assembled ships. The originals' recorded message—pleading for their copies to be raised, not studied—turns the fleets' greed into shame. The colonists, led by the children, claim all seven as their own. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging chosen over invisibility, inheritance reclaimed as gift rather than burden.
